questions.question:
Study the graph which shows the target and actual production of ACs, (in thousands) of a factory over five months and answer the question that follows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/425aee544cdada9a88b0fcf207d9cd05715870e25c4098908ce306b2d8c39418.png] 

The total target production of ACs in February, March, April, and May is what percent less than the total actual production of ACs over five months? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Total target production of ACs in February, March, April and May = 30 + 80 + 90 + 100 = 300(in thousands)

Total actual production of ACs over five months = 70 + 50 + 100 + 80 + 120 = 420(in thousands)

Their difference = 420 – 300 = 120

Required % = 120/420 × 100 = 28.57% ∼ 28.6%

**∴ The required % is 28.6%**

The number of students enrolled in different streams at Senior Secondary level in five schools has been shown in the bar graph.

What percentage of the total number of students in all the streams taken together in all the five schools to the number of students enrolled in the science stream in school A?

questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

The number of students enrolled in the science stream in school A = 60

Total number of students in school A = (60 + 70 + 50) = 180

Total number of students in school B = (78 + 82 + 40) = 200

Total number of students in school C = (45 + 40 + 35) = 120

Total number of students in school D = (40 + 45 + 40) = 125

Total number of students in school E = (40 + 35 + 50) = 125

Now,

The total number of students in all the streams taken together in all the five schools = (180 + 200 + 120 + 125 + 125) = 750

The percentage of the total number of students in all the streams taken together in all the five schools is the number of students enrolled in the science stream in school A = (60/750 × 100)

questions.question:
The givengraph shows the higher secondary result of a particular school, from 2019 to 2021. Study the graph and answer the question that follows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93f8691f8f3f5dbd4c28adc5312b9766858dd2d9de9ecbfa5ec948bd93e9fcf4.png] 

The percentage of students who passed in the year 2020 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The graph shows the higher secondary result of a particular school for the years 2019, 2020, and 2021. The total percentage of students who passed in the year 2020 is required.

**Formula used:**

Percentage of students who passed = [(Total students passed in First, Second, and Third Divisions) / (Total students)] * 100

**Calculation:**

In 2020, from the graph:

First Division: 70

Second Division: 80

Third Division: 95

Failed: 5

Total students = 70 + 80 + 95 + 5 = 250

Students who passed = 70 + 80 + 95 = 245

⇒ Percentage of students who passed = (245 / 250) × 100 = 98%

**∴ The correct answer is option (1), 98%.**

The bar graph given below shows the cost price and value of profit of 6 articles A, B, C, D, E and F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76c5fbaeac1bcb8065b72f61a66837a22967e7c966bd5c88e96f20d977cc0b33.png] 

Selling price = Cost price + Profit

P1 = The difference between the total cost price and total profit.

P2 = The difference between the total cost price of A and B and the total selling price of E and F

What is the value of (P1 - P2)?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Total Cost Price = 750 + 650 + 450 + 550 + 350 + 850 = 3600

Total Profit = 250 + 200 + 350 + 450 + 300 + 400 = 1950

P1 = 3600 - 1950 = 1650

The total cost price of A and B = 750 + 650 = 1400

The total selling price of E and F = 350 + 300 + 850 + 400 = 1900

P2 = 1900 - 1400 = 500

P1 - P2 = 1650 - 500 = 1150

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

In the year 2019, if the imports increased by the same percentage as that in 2018 over its previous year, then what was the amount (in Rs. crores) of the imports in the year 2019?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**The percentage can be converted into ratio.

**Traditional method:**

**Given:**

⇒ Percentage increase of imports in 2019 = 100/9 % 

⇒ (y - Imports in 2018)/y ×100 = 100/9 

⇒ (y - 450)/y = 1/9 

⇒ y = 9 × (y - 450)

⇒ y - 9y = - 9 × 450 

⇒ - 8y = - 9 × 450 

⇒ y = 9 × 450/8 

⇒ y = 506.25

**∴ The imports in the year 2019 was of Rs.506.25 crores.**

questions.question: In the given histogram, in which class interval, the median lies?
questions.solution:
If number of the observation is n is odd, then the median is [(n + 1)/2]th observation.

If number of the observation is n is even, then the median will be the average of the (n/2)th and [(n/2 + 1)]th observation.

Total number of students = 50 + 70 + 85 + 90 + 60 + 45 = 400

Median = [(400/2) + (400/2) + 1)]2 = (200 + 201)/2 = 200.5th (201th) students (which comes in 60 - 70)

Number of students who lies (40 - 50) = 50 students

Number of students who lies (50 - 60) = 70 students = 51th to 120th

Number of students who lies (60 - 70) = 85 students = 121th to 205th

So, 200.5th (201th) students comes in 60 - 70.
